import pandas as pd

# Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_56/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_56/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_56/training_2.csv"
source3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_56/training_3.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)
df3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path, index_col=0)

# Operation History:
# 1) JOIN : [["Source3_56_0", "Source3_56_2"], ["CountyID", "CountyID"], ["Year", "Year"]]
# 2) JOIN : [["Source3_56_1", "Source3_56_3"], ["CountyID", "CountyID"], ["Year", "Year"]]
# 3) JOIN : [["Source3_56_0", "Source3_56_3"], ["CountyID", "CountyID"], ["Year", "Year"]]

# Step 1: Join Source0 and Source2 on CountyID and Year
# To avoid column name collisions, pandas will add suffixes _x and _y automatically
join_0_2 = pd.merge(
    df0,
    df2,
    how="inner",
    left_on=["CountyID", "Year"],
    right_on=["CountyID", "Year"],
    suffixes=('_x', '_y')
)

# Step 2: Join Source1 and Source3 on CountyID and Year
join_1_3 = pd.merge(
    df1,
    df3,
    how="inner",
    left_on=["CountyID", "Year"],
    right_on=["CountyID", "Year"],
    suffixes=('_x', '_y')
)

# Step 3: Join Source0 and Source3 on CountyID and Year
join_0_3 = pd.merge(
    df0,
    df3,
    how="inner",
    left_on=["CountyID", "Year"],
    right_on=["CountyID", "Year"],
    suffixes=('_x_9', '_y_14')
)

# Now join the results according to the operation history sequence:
# The final target schema has columns from all these joins combined.
# The last join in operation history is between Source0 and Source3,
# but we need to combine all three join results into one DataFrame.

# To combine these three join results, we join join_0_2 and join_1_3 first,
# then join the result with join_0_3.

# Join join_0_2 and join_1_3 on CountyID and Year columns.
# But note join_0_2 has CountyID_x, Year_x and CountyID_y, Year_y,
# join_1_3 has CountyID_x, Year_x and CountyID_y, Year_y as well.
# We need to pick consistent keys to join on.

# We'll join join_0_2 and join_1_3 on:
# join_0_2: CountyID_x and Year_x
# join_1_3: CountyID_x and Year_x

combined_0_2__1_3 = pd.merge(
    join_0_2,
    join_1_3,
    how="inner",
    left_on=["CountyID_x", "Year_x"],
    right_on=["CountyID_x", "Year_x"],
    suffixes=('', '_drop')  # to avoid duplicate columns, drop duplicates later
)

# Drop duplicated columns from join_1_3 that are already in join_0_2
cols_to_drop = [col for col in combined_0_2__1_3.columns if col.endswith('_drop')]
combined_0_2__1_3.drop(columns=cols_to_drop, inplace=True)

# Now join combined_0_2__1_3 with join_0_3 on CountyID and Year columns.
# join_0_3 has CountyID_x_9 and Year_x_12 (from Source0) and CountyID_y_14 and Year_y_16 (from Source3)
# We join on Source0 keys: CountyID_x (from combined_0_2__1_3) and CountyID_x_9 (from join_0_3)
# and Year_x (from combined_0_2__1_3) and Year_x_12 (from join_0_3)

final_df = pd.merge(
    combined_0_2__1_3,
    join_0_3,
    how="inner",
    left_on=["CountyID_x", "Year_x"],
    right_on=["CountyID_x_9", "Year_x_12"]
)

# Now we need to select and rename columns to match the target schema exactly:
# Target Schema:
# ['CountyID_x': int, 'CountyName_x': str, 'whites_population': int, 'Year_x': int, 'ID': int,
#  'CountyID_y': int, 'CountyName_y': str, 'other_population': int, 'Year_y': int,
#  'CountyID_x_9': int, 'CountyName_x_10': str, 'mixed_population': int, 'Year_x_12': int,
#  'CountyID_y_13': int, 'CountyName_y_14': str, 'asian_population': int, 'Year_y_16': int]

# Columns from join_0_2:
# CountyID_x, CountyName_x, whites_population, Year_x, ID (from Source0)
# CountyID_y, CountyName_y, other_population, Year_y, ID_y (from Source2) - ID_y not needed in target

# Columns from join_1_3:
# CountyID_x, CountyName_x, asian_population, Year_x, ID (from Source1)
# CountyID_y, CountyName_y, mixed_population, Year_y, ID_y (from Source3) - ID_y not needed in target

# Columns from join_0_3:
# CountyID_x_9, CountyName_x_10, whites_population_9?, Year_x_12, ID_9 (from Source0)
# CountyID_y_13, CountyName_y_14, mixed_population_14?, Year_y_16, ID_14 (from Source3)

# But we already have whites_population and mixed_population from previous joins,
# so we take asian_population from join_1_3 and mixed_population from join_0_3 as per target schema.

# To avoid confusion, let's carefully pick columns from final_df:

result = pd.DataFrame()

# From join_0_2 (Source0 and Source2)
result['CountyID_x'] = final_df['CountyID_x']
result['CountyName_x'] = final_df['CountyName_x']
result['whites_population'] = final_df['whites_population']
result['Year_x'] = final_df['Year_x']
result['ID'] = final_df['ID']  # from Source0

result['CountyID_y'] = final_df['CountyID_y']
result['CountyName_y'] = final_df['CountyName_y']
result['other_population'] = final_df['other_population']
result['Year_y'] = final_df['Year_y']

# From join_0_3 (Source0 and Source3)
result['CountyID_x_9'] = final_df['CountyID_x_9']
result['CountyName_x_10'] = final_df['CountyName_x_10']
result['mixed_population'] = final_df['mixed_population']
result['Year_x_12'] = final_df['Year_x_12']

result['CountyID_y_13'] = final_df['CountyID_y_13']
result['CountyName_y_14'] = final_df['CountyName_y_14']
result['asian_population'] = final_df['asian_population']
result['Year_y_16'] = final_df['Year_y_16']

# Ensure correct dtypes as per target schema
result = result.astype({
    'CountyID_x': 'int64',
    'CountyName_x': 'string',
    'whites_population': 'int64',
    'Year_x': 'int64',
    'ID': 'int64',
    'CountyID_y': 'int64',
    'CountyName_y': 'string',
    'other_population': 'int64',
    'Year_y': 'int64',
    'CountyID_x_9': 'int64',
    'CountyName_x_10': 'string',
    'mixed_population': 'int64',
    'Year_x_12': 'int64',
    'CountyID_y_13': 'int64',
    'CountyName_y_14': 'string',
    'asian_population': 'int64',
    'Year_y_16': 'int64'
})

# Write the result to the target CSV file
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_56/target_multisource.csv"
result.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

    source0,
    source2,
    how="inner",
    on=["CountyID", "Year"],
    suffixes=("_x", "_y")
)

# Then join the above result with Source3 on CountyID and Year
df_0_2_3 = pd.merge(
    df_0_2,
    source3,
    how="inner",
    on=["CountyID", "Year"],
    suffixes=("", "_x_10")
)

# Finally join the above result with Source1 on CountyID and Year

    df_0_2_3,
    source1,

    on=["CountyID", "Year"],
    suffixes=("_y_14", "_y_16")
